text: Re-read 2026-08-17. The version-gated extraction comments are exact: tar.extractall runs with filter='data' where the stdlib supports it (3.12+) and falls back to the pre-validated member list with the noqa marker below, so 'members are already validated and mode-normalized; pass the stdlib filter too for belt and braces' describes both branches truthfully. 'Derived is replaced; authored is merged' still matches DERIVED_DIRS and _merge_meta. The injectable fetch is still what makes the whole path testable without network - the file:// bundle validation in the 0.55.1 acceptance ran through exactly that seam.

author: cli
text: Re-read at 0.57.0. Every earlier claim holds: injectable fetch, version-gated extractall, derived replaced and authored merged, and the member validation that makes the four attack falsifications meaningful. NEW: replay=True inverts what gets installed. The default hands you the bundle's INDEX, which describes the commit it was built from - so a checkout anywhere else holds a map of code it does not have, with drifted:true as the whole response. With replay the local tree is indexed and only the KNOWLEDGE crosses, matched by coordinate and, where names moved, by lineage.score_pair at its own 0.55 threshold. Replayed entries keep their ORIGINAL stamps, which is the property that makes it safe: a note written against v1 reads stale on v2 when its code moved and current when it did not, so version skew becomes a question rather than a false claim. Two things this surfaced: the bundle's manifest dies with its index, so provenance has to be carried out before the temp dir goes (without it 'drifted' read False on the one case that is always a drift), and the drift SENTENCE had to fork - on a replay the map is yours and it is the knowledge that came from elsewhere, where the install wording printed 'this map describes None'.
